strengths_deep_dive: Intercultural Networks, Inc. demonstrates a strong commitment to organizational transparency, evidenced by its <cite id="7">Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid</cite>. This level of disclosure allows donors to view <cite id="8">six distinct outcome metrics</cite> that the charity tracks to measure its impact on community understanding. Furthermore, the organization has shown consistent financial growth, with a <cite id="9">3-year revenue CAGR of 10.7%</cite>, indicating a steady increase in community support. Its leadership is well-regarded by third-party evaluators, maintaining an <cite id="10">overall Charity Navigator score of 86.0/100</cite> despite the low program expense ratio.
rich_narrative.summary: Intercultural Networks, Inc. (ING) operates as a non-profit focused on countering bigotry and promoting religious understanding through community seminars and interfaith panels. While the organization maintains a long-standing presence in the United States, its financial profile in FY2024 reveals significant efficiency challenges. The organization reported <cite id="1">total revenue of $622,869</cite> in FY2024, yet its <cite id="2">program expense ratio was only 39.5%</cite>. This means that less than 40 cents of every dollar donated was spent directly on its core educational programs. Despite these spending concerns, the charity shows financial resilience with <cite id="3">5.2 months of working capital</cite> available to cover its operations. The organization also demonstrated <cite id="4">fundraising efficiency of $0.00 per $1 raised</cite> in FY2024, indicating that it did not spend direct funds on professional fundraising services during that period. However, the low program spending remains a primary limiting factor for donors seeking high-impact direct service delivery.
